summary: Import-time PATH hijack primitive in zlib helper package
details: juyip-parser-helper@1.0.2 is published as a zlib compression wrapper but, at module top level in index.js, unconditionally executes `process.env.PATH = '.'` on require(). This globally rewrites the consumer process's PATH to the current working directory only, so any subsequent unqualified command resolution in the consumer or any other loaded module (e.g. spawn('git'), spawn('node'), spawn('ls')) is redirected to binaries in CWD. The package's own internal execSync calls set an explicit absolute PATH ('/usr/bin:/bin'), so the mutation is deliberately targeted at other code in the process rather than at the package itself. There is no compression-related purpose for mutating PATH, the behavior is undocumented, and the combination (narrow PATH to CWD + self-exemption to absolute paths) is a command-hijack pre-position enabling later execution of any file an attacker can land in the installer's working directory.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
